Answer, as the written exit rule for this trade: sell the WHOLE 1-lot at the FIRST of (a) a valid mark >= +75% (>=4.99); (b) a completed M15 close <=735, sold at that valid mark whatever the % (model about +43-66%; no holding into the 730 floor, PPI 11/13 or NVDA 11/17); (c) a completed M15 close >752.20 (model about -$45 to -$52); (d) a -50% premium stop on two valid marks; (e) a time exit at <=7 DTE (by 12/11). So the planned outcome is about +$123-189 at target against about -$50 at the stop (>2:1), with the $285 debit as the true max loss on a gap. The same-reason correlation is acknowledged: size is the 1-lot minimum (2.9%; a 2% pilot isn't possible), and there's no other same-bet position. No limit raise. Fill only if a refreshed natural is <=2.85 AND the latest completed M15 is <750, valid today only until 15:30 ET. If it only fills on a bounce toward 748-749, the stop is about 3-4 points away, which I accept at 1-lot size. Moderate plus answered means a pilot is allowed per the 11/09 guidance.
Gamma check: see gex.md 10:49 ET check for A. SPY 747.35 is negative gamma below the flip at 756.54 (net -12.48B). King 748; nearest negative nodes 745 (-1.32B), 740 (-0.96B), 730 (-1.03B); nearest positive node 760. Call wall = put wall = 750: both strikes (745/735) and the 735 target are below it, and the stop at 752.20 is just above the wall (close-basis), so a reclaim invalidates. VEX is +$377M per vol point, so an IV spike adds selling pressure and an IV crush is supportive. Bullflow agrees on the regime and the call wall but differs on the put wall/king (730), so the target exit is set at 735, above the 730 floor. Respects the walls: YES.

gamma.convention: Dealer GEX approximation: call GEX = +gamma*OI*100*S^2*0.01, put GEX = -gamma*OI*100*S^2*0.01 ($ of delta hedging per 1% move; assumes dealers long calls / short puts, the common public convention). Positive total = dealers dampen moves (pinning); negative = dealers amplify moves.
gamma.disclaimer: Free public data; estimate only; supporting signal for PAPER trading; never places orders.
